mechanism.claim: A corporate-credit polarity transition transmits in its new direction when completed BTC seven-day variation is expanding versus the prior source-valid session, but represents a normalization fade when that variation is contracting. Route the credit transition by the causal variation phase for twenty-four hours.
mechanism.side: credit-transition sign multiplied by strict sign of current minus previous completed BTC variation
mechanism.why_distinct: HVCQTR trades credit polarity transitions with a fixed side and failed test. HVCQVAR is a cross-domain router that combines the same predecision transition object with the independently completed BTC variation phase. It uses no HVCREDIT event set/control, equity return, Treasury price, crypto direction, OI, funding, premium, options, fitted outcome, or promoted control.
mechanism.why_low_gross9_overlap_is_plausible: external credit transitions routed by crypto volatility phase are absent from Gross9

features.relative_credit_return: log(HYG close/open)-log(LQD close/open), finite strict nonzero
features.previous: immediately prior source-valid shared cash session in frozen chronological order
features.transition: current and previous relative returns have strict opposite signs
features.variation_phase: strict sign of current btc_variation minus immediately previous source-valid btc_variation; zero is cash

clock.reservation: chronological half-open nonoverlap; exit first on equal entry
clock.funding: not signal input; exact settlements after Gross9

economic_gates.accounting: fixed quantity, exact funding, 6bp base and 10bp stress per notional side, every held 5m favorable then adverse, global HWM, full-calendar CAGR

research_boundary.classification: exploratory discovery; not fresh confirmatory evidence
research_boundary.selection_basis: credit transition conditioned by independent BTC variation phase

stopping_rule: source, Gross9, train/test/eval/final; terminal first failure; no assets, return, previous-session law, transition, variation phase, side, clock, hold, subset, comparator, or control repair
